> **FLUID-ICU is SIMULATED.** Say so every time you open the data: no real patient, hospital or country. All numbers below are from `Course/Data/key_results.md` and `Course/Data/cleaning_log.md`.


* * *

## Before the session (night before + 10 minutes before)

- [ ] R (4.x) and RStudio installed on the projector laptop; packages: tidyverse, janitor, gtsummary, flextable, survival, survminer, mice, broom.
- [ ] Open `Course/Data/FLUID-ICU.Rproj` (sets the working folder). Run `01_clean.R` and `02_describe.R` once end to end; both must finish without error.
- [ ] Increase the editor and console font (Tools → Global Options → Appearance → 18–20 pt) so the back row can read.
- [ ] Keep the fallback figures open in an image viewer: `Course/Resources/figures/en/data/` (`raw_vs_clean.png`, `table1_snapshot.png`, `fluid_balance_hist.png`, `sofa_by_group.png`, `los_skewed.png`) and `Course/Data/output/figures/`.
- [ ] Open `Course/Data/cleaning_log.md` and `data_dictionary.md` in a browser tab: you will show them.

**Rules of the demo:** run one block at a time (Ctrl+Enter); before each block, ask the room *"what do you expect?"*; after it, say *what was fixed and that it goes in the log*. Never type new code live — the scripts are complete.


* * *

## Part A — From raw to clean (01_clean.R, 8 minutes)

| Step (script block) | What you show | Expected output | Say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Read raw as text | `dim(raw)`, `glimpse(raw)` | **623 rows**, 29 columns, everything `<chr>` | "The study enrolled 620 patients. Why 623 rows?" |
| 1. Column names | `names(dat)` | short lower-case names (`map_mmhg`, `vent_free_days_28`) | "Names without spaces: same in every script." |
| 2. Duplicates | `get_dupes(study_id)` | 3 study IDs appear twice, identical rows; after `distinct()` **620** | "Each patient counted once." |
| 3. Sites | `count(site)` before/after | variants such as `icu a`, `ICU-A` → 4 sites | "Otherwise R sees many different ICUs." |
| 4. Dates | the three formats | `2023-03-14`, `14/03/2023`, `14-Mar-2023` → one date; 0 failures | "Is 03/04 March or April? Never guess." |
| 5–6. Sex and yes/no | `tabyl()` before/after | many spellings (M, m, male, F, f, " Female"; Y, 1, yes) → `Male/Female`, `Yes/No` | "1 and Yes must mean the same thing." |
| 7–8. Numbers and codes | `summary()` of lactate, MAP, APACHE II | maxima of **999**, minima of **-99** → set to NA | "A lactate of 999 would wreck the mean." |
| 9. Units | lactate median **by ICU** | ICU C about 9 times higher (mg/dL) → divided by 9.01 | "Found only because we summarised by ICU. Ask the site lab." |
| 10. Impossible values | range checks | age 210, weight 7 kg, a negative fluid output → NA + query; patient kept | "We cannot guess 21 or 71. We never delete the patient." |
| 12. Derived variables | the fluid-balance formula | `cum_fluid_balance_d3_ml_kg`, `positive_balance_d3`, `aki_any` computed | "Derived values are calculated, never typed." |
| 13. What is left | `colSums(is.na(dat))` | lactate 93 missing; a handful elsewhere | "These are REAL gaps; we handle them in Session 6." |
| 14. Reproducibility | final `cat()` | `Cleaned data identical to the reference clean file: TRUE` / `byte-for-byte identical: TRUE` | "Anyone can re-run this and get exactly the same data." |

**If short of time:** run Steps 0, 2, 9, 10 and 14 only (4 minutes) and show the cleaning log for the rest.

**Close Part A** by opening `cleaning_log.md`: *"Every block you saw is one row here: problem, how many, what we did, why."* Then show the slide *From 623 rows to 527 complete cases* (620 enrolled → 618 with a day-3 balance → 527 complete cases).

## Part B — Table 1 and figures (02_describe.R, 6 minutes)

| Block | What you show | Expected output (key_results.md) | Say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Load | `dim(icu)`, `count(positive_balance_d3)` | 620 patients; positive balance **373/618 (60.4%)**; 2 without a balance | "618, not 620: two patients have no computable balance." |
| 2. Shape first | mean/SD of age, median/IQR of lactate; quick histograms | age mean **62.6 (SD 15.2)**; lactate skewed | "Symmetric → mean (SD); skewed → median (IQR)." |
| 3. Table 1 | the gtsummary table by group | negative n = 245, positive n = 373; SOFA **6 (4 to 8) vs 8 (6 to 10)**; vasopressor **24.9% vs 55.0%**; ventilation **39.6% vs 57.9%**; lactate **2.2 vs 2.9** mmol/L; heart failure **22.0% vs 11.5%**; missing counts shown; **no p-values** | "Were the groups alike at the start? No: the positive group was sicker." |
| 4. Histogram | fluid balance by group | median **8.8 ml/kg (IQR -10.3 to 26.2)** | "Continuous exposure, cut at 0." |
| 5. Boxplot | SOFA by group, with dots | medians 6 vs 8 | "Show every patient." |
| 6. Bar chart | infection source, sorted | respiratory most common | "Categories → sorted bars, not a 3-D pie." |
| 7. Outcomes | described, not compared | 28-day mortality **179/620 (28.9%)**; ICU stay mean 7.3 vs median 6.0 days | "Described today, compared tomorrow." |

**Close Part B:** *"This Table 1 is in every group's results pack. Your worksheet now: read it as a reviewer would."* → Exercise 6.

## Fallback plan

| Problem | Do this |
|---|---|
| R or a package fails | Show `raw_vs_clean.png` and talk through the problems (Part A); show `table1_snapshot.png`, `fluid_balance_hist.png`, `sofa_by_group.png` (Part B). Teaching points are identical. |
| Projector cannot show RStudio legibly | Use the PNG figures and `cleaning_log.md` in a browser at 150% zoom. |
| Running late | Part A: Steps 0, 2, 9, 10, 14. Part B: blocks 3 and 5 only. |
| A participant asks to run it themselves | Point to `Course/Data/README.md` and the free *Clinical Data Analysis in R* course; offer to help after the session. |

## Anticipated questions

**"Is this real data?"** No — simulated, designed to behave like ICU data and to show the classic problems. Any manuscript must say so.

**"Why not fix the errors in Excel?"** Hand edits leave no trace and cannot be repeated; one wrong paste is invisible. A script plus a log is checkable by a reviewer and repeatable by anyone.

**"Why set age 210 to missing instead of guessing 21?"** It could be 21, 71 or 10; guessing invents data. Set to missing, query the site, correct only with the source document.

**"Why no p-values in Table 1?"** Table 1 describes the groups. The SAP says so explicitly; in an RCT any difference is chance, in a cohort it is confounding to be adjusted for, not tested.
